title: Deep ComCat pairs showed no clear extra depth similarity after a surface-spacing check in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested depth similarity in 785 ComCat earthquakes with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth greater than 300 km in 2000-2025. In 143 pairs within 100 km at the surface and seven days in the same year, the mean absolute depth difference was 27.65 km. Time shuffles within year and 10-degree cells gave 33.17 km and a lower-tail p-value of 0.0285 in 9,999 draws. A 20-degree grid gave p = 0.0662. Observed pairs were also closer at the surface. A post hoc check that subtracted mean depth gaps in 25 km surface-distance bins gave p = 0.2137. A post hoc check with no shared events gave p = 0.0928. Thus extra depth similarity remains uncertain. These checks do not establish that surface spacing explains all of the original difference. Overlapping data, sparse large events, location errors, mixed magnitude scales, revised catalog records and time-exchangeability assumptions limit inference. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence, figures, source hashes and an independent numerical audit. Raw and record-level data remain external.
